meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/05, Monday 3 June 2024). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: June 2024 series, despite the download folder's Nov 24 label. Coded in the same sitting as OCR-JUN24-F-P2, its non-calculator Foundation partner. Interleaved crossover: J560/02 q17, q18, q21, q22 and q23 reappear here as q1, q2, q3, q4 and q10, with marks matching item for item (2, 4, 7, 8, 4 — 25 of the 100). J560/02 q20 and this paper's q11 are BOTH vector questions on the same grid but they are NOT the same item: /02 q20 is worth 3 marks and asks for a column vector and a multiple, while q11 here is worth 6 and adds an equal-length vector and a resultant to draw. No per-question total is printed, so the whole-paper sum against the published 100 is the only check, and this file passes it.

coding_notes: q1, q2, q3, q4 and q10 are J560/02 q17, q18, q21, q22 and q23 and carry identical skill tags, kinds and mark splits to that file, by design.
mark_split is derived from OCR's part totals and partial-credit routes rather than quoted; see OCR-JUN24-F-P1 for the reasoning.

q4b is the outlier-identification item flagged in OCR-JUN24-F-P2's notes — tagged scatter_graphs there and here, against the 2026-09-04 ruling that left a range/mean outlier item untagged. Both copies move together if that ruling is extended.

q6 tagged estimating before compound_units, matching the handling of every other 'round first, then calculate' item in the audit. OCR-JUN25-H-P5 q11 put compound_units first on a similar density item; that row is the outlier, not this one.

q9 tagged substitution alone, although the route runs through two of the three given kinematics formulas in turn. The demand is substituting into formulas that are printed for the student, not knowing the relationships.
q12b tagged growth_and_decay then exponential_graphs: the multiplier b comes from two values one year apart, and the graph is how they are given.

q17 tagged recurring_decimals_to_fractions first — the mark scheme's main route works in recurring decimals and its alternative converts the recurring decimal to a fraction, and either way that conversion is the step the item exists for.

q20 tagged sector_calculations then exact_trig_values then surds_simplifying: the answer's a√b + kπ form needs the exact cosine of 30° and a simplified surd, and the mark scheme awards a B1 specifically for that trig value.
